articles.title: WNBA Finals predictions: Valkyries or Dream? Our experts make their picks
articles.summary: A new WNBA champion will be crowned before the month is over. The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will match up for the best-of-seven finals, starti...
articles.body:
A new WNBA champion will be crowned before the month is over.

The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will match up for the best-of-seven finals, starting on Oct. 17. The Valkyries, in just their second season after they kick-started the WNBA's wave of expansion, are a surprise to many but have all the makings of a title contender. The Dream, who had previously been the youngest sibling in the league after its 2008 founding, hasn't been to the championship round since 2013 and has never won there.

The title contenders get a break, some time to recover before their championship bout. But not our experts at The Athletic .

Our playoff reporters are thinking about how this series will play out — and they think they've got the answers.

Who do you have? Let us know in the comments.

The 2026 WNBA Finals comes down to, just as everyone predicted, the Valkyries and the Dream. Two defensive juggernauts dueling it out for a piece of history.

After watching a three-game sweep of the Liberty, courtesy of the Dream, my pick for the finals winner is Atlanta. The Dream put on a masterclass against the Liberty and did so without leading scorer Allisha Gray, who sustained a left hand injury in Game 1 of the semifinals. The offensive production from Jordin Canada and DeWanna Bonner showed a level of depth that will be hard to contend with for a team with the seventh-best offense in the league.

The regular-season sweep by Golden State means nothing. We can get that out of the way. But I do think the distance from it — these teams last played on July 4 — can be a factor. The Valkyries' energy and effort is just different, and it has two home games as a launching pad. Any idea that they're not totally ready for the postseason pressure cooker went out the door in Las Vegas on Friday night.

Atlanta will play better defense than Las Vegas did, but the Dream don't have better individual scorers. Over time, Golden State's defense and depth of talent wins out.

I've picked against the Dream in two consecutive rounds only to have Atlanta sweep the Mystics and Liberty. I am not going to make the same mistake again. Yes, Golden State went 3-0 against Atlanta during the regular season, but the addition of DeWanna Bonner has been key and made Atlanta's defense that much scarier. Plus, the Dream's regular-season leading scorer Gray, who played only two quarters in this series, will be extremely rested when she's healthy and able to return.

Don't be fooled by the Valkyries' undefeated record against Atlanta this season. Both teams have found a different stride since. Both teams are brimming with confidence after eliminating legends. Canada is playing exceptional hoop, and Angel Reese is a true gamer. But the depth and versatility of the Valkyries, and their home court advantage, gives them a slight edge. Plus, Golden State has the best player in the series in Gabby Williams. If Gray misses too much time, that works in the Valkyries' favor.

articles.title: Dream set to play WNBA Finals home games at smaller Gateway Center Arena, rather than State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta
articles.summary: The Dream are exploring other large venues in the Atlanta area, as State Farm Arena has events booked for the dates of Games 3, 4 and 6 of the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
After playing three home playoff games at State Farm Arena during their run to the WNBA Finals, the Atlanta Dream is faced with hosting games for the league's championship series at the smaller Gateway Center Arena.

The Dream played six of their 22 home games during the regular season at the larger State Farm Arena, home to the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. With a capacity of 16,888 for basketball games, the larger facility could accommodate what were certain to be bigger crowds for two WNBA Finals games.

Additionally, State Farm Arena is located in downtown Atlanta, presumably providing easier access from hotels, highways and mass transit, in addition to more parking and ability to walk to the stadium from the city center.

Instead, the Dream will have to play at the smaller Gateway Center Arena, which seats 3,500 for basketball games and is located just outside Atlanta in College Park, Georgia.

By comparison, the Golden State Valkyries will host Games 1, 2, 5 and 7 at Chase Center in San Francisco, also the home of the NBA's Golden State Warriors, which seats 18,064 for basketball .

The Dream have attempted to move their WNBA Finals games to a larger arena in the area, but have thus far been unsuccessful in those discussions, according to USA Today's Meghan L. Hall .

Among the other possible venues in the Atlanta metropolitan area are McCavish Pavilion on the campus of Georgia Tech, which can seat 8,600 for basketball games. The Convocation Center at Georgia State University also has a capacity of 7,500 for basketball.

Gas South Arena in Duluth, Georgia — located nearly 30 miles from downtown Atlanta — can accommodate 12,750 and is also being considered. The Dream played Game 3 of the 2013 WNBA Finals at that facility.

State Farm Arena is unavailable for Games 3, 4 and 6 of the WNBA Finals — scheduled for Oct. 22, Oct. 24 and Oct. 29, respectively — with a concert by Sombr and two Hawks regular-season games , including the team's home opener, already booked at the venue.

"We didn't have playoff games [at State Farm Arena] last year... but we had a couple of games there, and they felt like playoff games," Dream guard Rhyne Howard told USA Today . "So I think for us to have had those during the season and have the outcome that we had, I think it helps us get ready for this environment."

Last week, the Dream announced that they will play all of their 2027 home games at State Farm Arena . Each team will have 25 home games as part of an expanded 50-game WNBA regular-season schedule. However, that obviously does nothing to solve the problem of what to do during the WNBA Finals.

articles.title: Deck será operado y estará de baja entre cinco y seis meses
articles.standfirst: Sufre una inestabilidad anterior en el hombro izquierdo, tras episodio de luxación articular
articles.summary: Sufre una inestabilidad anterior en el hombro izquierdo, tras episodio de luxación articular
articles.body: Un año más las lesiones visitan a Gabriel Deck. En este caso no es para terminar su temporada, como las roturas de ligamentos de la rodilla como en 2023 y 2024 o la de cadera de 2024 a 2025, sino para complicar el comienzo de la nueva. Gabriel Deck sufre una inestabilidad anterior en el hombro izquierdo, tras episodio de luxación articular, tal y como indica el parte médico del Real Madrid, y deberá pasar por el quirófano en los próximos días. No hay tiempo oficial de baja, pero se estima que en este tipo de lesiones en el hombro, entre recuperación y puesta a punto el tiempo sin jugar sea de entre cinco y seis meses, si la operación no tiene complicaciones. Eso quiere decir que Deck no reaparecerá, como mínimo, hasta mediados de marzo, eso si se cumplen los tiempos. El argentino por lo tanto se perderá la Copa del Rey, pero sí estará en el tramo final de la temporada, cuando el Madrid esté buscando una buena clasificación en la Liga regular de cara a intentar meterse en la Final Four y para los Playoffs de la Liga Endesa. El problema es que Deck es un jugador al que le cuesta coger la forma y por lo tanto tardará más en entrar en la dinámica de su equipo. Habrá que ver si el Madrid decide acudir al mercado para tratar de fichar a un jugador que sustituya de forma provisional al argentino. Deck había comenzado la temporada en buen estado, rindiendo a buen nivel en la SuperCup de la Euroliga en Abu Dabi, y esta lesión, producida en la concentración de la selección de Argentina en las últimas Ventanas, es un enorme palo para él y también para el Madrid por la importancia del jugador en cuanto a intensidad, prestaciones defensivas y aportación en ataque.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Armani Milán - Real Madrid: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el partido de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: El Madrid busca su primer triunfo fuera del Movistar Arena
articles.summary: El Madrid busca su primer triunfo fuera del Movistar Arena
articles.body: Tres de tres es el balance que luce el Madrid en sus salidas en la Euroliga. El año pasado llegó a perder sus cuatro primeros partidos fuera ante de ganar en el Palau en la jornada 9. De hecho, de los equipos de Playoffs, los blancos eran el equipo con peor balance fuera de casa (6-13). Esa poca fiabilidad a la hora de jugar lejos del Movistar Arena es lo que más llenó de incertidumbre la temporada blanca. Para evitar esos problemas, los de Pedro Martínez necesitar acabar con esa asignatura pendiente cuanto antes. El Madrid visita al colista, Armani MIlán, donde ha perdido en sus tres últimas visitas. Pero en esta ocasión el equipo de Giuseppe Poeta atraviesa un periodo complicado. Tiene el mismo balance que el Madrid, pero las sensaciones son diferentes. En su último partido cayó con estrépito en Tel Aviv ante el Maccbi, 91-79, y ha jugado ante cuatro rivales que seguramente no estarán en los Playoffs en abril (el propio Maccabi, el Baskonia, la Virtus y el Partizan). Los blancos acuden con la baja de Deck. Ya se sabía que no jugaría en Milán, pero eso era todo. Ahora la ausencia será por casi seis meses después de que se confirmara que pasará por el quirófano para reparar una lesión en el hombro izquierdo. Varapalo para el argentino y para el Madrid, que pierde una pieza clave. Pedro Martínez, en la previa del partido, habló de su próximo rival: “Es un equipo que tiene muchísima variabilidad táctica en su defensa, hacen muchísimas cosas diferentes. Tenemos que estar leyendo y adaptándonos a todas las cosas que van a ir haciendo. Hemos de ser fieles a los valores que entrenamos y a la identidad que queremos tener. Y pensar que tenemos que ir mejorando cosas con el día a día”. El encuentro entre el Armani Milán - Real Madrid, correspondiente a la quinta jornada de la Euroliga, se disputa este jueves 13 de octubre a las 20.30 horas (horario peninsular español) en el Unipol Forum de Milán. El partido entre el equipo blanco y el combinado serbio se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet a través de Movistar+. Y recuerda, puedes seguir toda la actualidad del baloncesto, el minuto a minuto del partido y la mejor crónica del Armani Milán - Real Madrid en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Lynx's Cheryl Reeve named WNBA Executive of the Year for record third time
articles.summary: Cheryl Reeve is taking home multiple awards in 2026.
articles.body:
Minnesota Lynx head coach and president of basketball operations Cheryl Reeve didn't just coach her team to a league-high 33 wins in 2026. She was also responsible for assembling the talent that propelled the team to the best record in the WNBA.

Because of that, Reeve was named the league's Executive of the Year on Monday.

The announcement comes just a few weeks after Reeve was named the WNBA Coach of the Year for a record fifth time.

Monday's award is also a record. With the win, Reeve tied Atlanta Dream Executive VP and GM Dan Padover as the only two individuals to win the award three times. Reeve also won the award in 2019 and 2024. Padover won the award in 2020 and 2021 with the Las Vegas Aces and then in 2025 with the Dream.

Following a tremendous year by the Dream, Padover nearly won the award for a fourth time. He came up just two votes short of Reeve, finishing in second for the award in 2026. Reeve appeared on 13 ballots. Padover was on 11 ballots. Ohemaa Nyanin of the Golden State Valkyries finished third in the voting.

Reeve's success in 2026 was largely due to the selection of star rookie Olivia Miles with the second overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. Miles turned in a fantastic first year, unanimously winning the Rookie of the Year award . Reeve also brought in veteran Natasha Howard, who returned to All-Star level in her first season with the Lynx.

Reeve was initially hired as the Lynx's head coach in 2010. She's remained in that role over the past 17 seasons, winning the WNBA championship four times. In addition to remaining the team's head coach, Reeve was promoted to general manager in 2017. In 2022, she was named the team's president of basketball operations.

articles.title: Why the Spurs are ready to make a bold tweak around Victor Wembanyama
articles.summary: San Antonio plans for De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper to start games together at some point.
articles.body:
After Victor Wembanyama returned to Frost Center for his first game in nearly four months, the fourth-year center was asked about his polarizing gravity. Not necessarily his adjustments or adaptations to how opposing teams build defensive game plans around him, but what his presence does for his teammates — particularly ball-handlers.

"It's the key to our offense," Wembanyama said. "We have so much talent and know where to put ourselves to give the other guys space. The key is being ready to score. It's easy when you space to forget that you're also playing, but you need to be a threat to bring the defense with you."

The distinction Wemby makes is important. While nothing is ironclad and the preseason is notorious for experimentation, the Spurs' willingness to move toward a three-guard lineup is palpable. Veteran guard De'Aaron Fox, who had popped up on the injury report last week due to general soreness, was held out of the past two preseason games vs. Atlanta and Phoenix, but at some point Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper will all share the floor to start games. Head coach Mitch Johnson isn't one to divulge more information than he's required to in public settings, but there's only so much grandstanding one can do in early October.

It's a bold tweak from a team that finished third in offensive and defensive efficiency last season, made it all the way to the Finals and held sizable leads in each of their losses. You could argue that the Spurs, who essentially kept the same team and added Tobias Harris, are in a perfect spot and don't need to overreact to their Finals heartbreak. This is a young group with a young coach in place that has an incredibly bright future ahead of them, injuries and drastic changes notwithstanding.

You could also, however, understand why Johnson would seek an extra organizer on the floor, especially given how chaotic San Antonio's fourth quarters were during the playoffs. The Spurs struggled to put games away in the final frame , often relying on individual moments of brilliance (or Wembyisms at the opportune time). In theory, that triumvirate brings different elements of their roster together and should maximize their offensive approach, both in the half-court and in transition. All three are capable of creating plays for others, albeit to varying degrees. There's also the notion of blending Fox's speed, Castle's physicality and Harper's combination of both. Such a unique concoction, in conjunction with Wembanyama's sheer presence and quality floor spacers — along with Harris' vast experience — should give the Spurs a clear run toward another deep playoff run.

But therein lies the challenge. In the modern game, which emphasizes spacing and efficient outside shooting, none of Fox, Harper or Castle have been consistent enough. Fox and Castle shot 33% from distance last season and Harper shot 34%. Yes, Fox and Harper connected on north of 40% of corner attempts, but neither generated nearly enough volume to warrant much defensive attention. It's also not a lineup that has seen much time together on the floor — or had success — with San Antonio being outscored by 21 points in 25 regular-season minutes and 26 in 44 postseason minutes.

Still, there's enough intrigue to understand just why Johnson feels comfortable taking the plunge. There's an increased importance on creating paint touches league-wide, given the propensity of defenses to collapse and the potential of drive-and-kick chances. What the likes of Harper and Castle lack in outside shooting, they more than make up for in downhill aggression and navigation, among the best in playoff points per paint touch , ahead of skilled centers like Alperen Şengün and Karl-Anthony Towns. The duo are also excellent rebounders at their position, with a knack for attacking angles without the ball with the same verve as they do with it. (Castle is a 96th percentile offensive rebounder, 76th for Harper . Fox is closer to league average.)

All roads lead back to Wemby. Through two preseason games, the Frenchman is second in attempted above-the-break 3s, per Second Spectrum, allowing Harper and Castle to roam underneath the arc and probe defenses. There have also been more frequent possessions with Wembanyama being a creator, further using his gravity to afford cuts from guards. Harper, while an infrequent cutter, was elite in that regard and Castle scored 1.29 points per possession last season. Given that both Fox and Harper are great around the rim ( 89th and 99th percentile respectively ), the easier things can become for Castle — who tends to overcomplicate at times — the better the trio will be overall.

"It's a delicate ecosystem," Johnson said. "We are well equipped when we have the proper spacing, pass the ball and are greedy for the right shots to pose problems to the defense. We just have to continue to find solutions because these teams in this league are very good and are going to take away first or second options a lot of times. That's going to test our discipline and execution."

Starting three guards would presumably slide Harris to power forward once he returns from a left calf strain. In the meantime, it appears that Devin Vassell will occupy that position. Johnson spoke highly of Vassell's leadership and growth, putting a great deal of faith in his ability to handle larger matchups. But this also would indicate that Julian Champagnie, who started 68 regular-season games and all 23 playoff games, would come off the bench. It's nothing short of a luxury for a fully healthy Spurs group to boast the spacing of those two in the second unit, but it's an adjustment nonetheless.

"No expectations," Champagnie told Yahoo Sports. "Whatever coach thinks is best for this team is what I think is best for this team. I'd run through a wall for all 18 guys here and the coaching staff. That's how I'm keeping it."

Such a shift requires strong team chemistry, which San Antonio has in spades. Being that close to achieving basketball immortality and falling short will only further motivate this group to get back to that point. The mental fortitude required to get through what is shaping up to be another grueling marathon is significant, but their attempt to zig while others zag could better illuminate their path to June.

"There's obviously a tweak this year," Champagnie said. "We're going to be hunted, so it's a little different. But one game at a time, one day at a time, don't get too ahead of ourselves. Don't dwell on the past. Win a couple, lose a couple and just stay in the moment."

articles.title: Las grietas que amenazan la construcción del nuevo Barça
articles.standfirst: Es el peor de la Euroliga en rebotes y asistencias, un déficit que lastra su juego, demasiado individualista en este inicio de curso
articles.summary: Es el peor de la Euroliga en rebotes y asistencias, un déficit que lastra su juego demasiado individualista
articles.body: El Barcelona (2-2) recibe este martes (20.30 h) al Maccabi Tel Aviv (1-3) en busca de su tercera victoria, aunque para ellos en los albores de esta temporada casi tan importante como el resultado es continuar creciendo en su juego, ganando solidez, regularidad y cohesión, algo nada sencillo cuando ha fichado a 11 jugadores y a un entrenador nuevo. Armar un puzzle con tantas piezas nuevas está alargando la fase de acoplamiento más de lo habitual, y justifica en gran parte las desconexiones que han sufrido los azulgranas en algunos partidos, y algunos errores y deficiencias explicables por esa incipiente adaptación y la falta de automatismos lógica entre jugadores que nunca antes habían jugado juntos, excepción hecha de Parra, Punter, Núñez y Brizuela. Algunos de los déficits de su juego han quedado al descubierto en este inicio de la Euroliga lastrando su rendimiento en determinados partidos y quedando de manifiesto en las estadísticas globales de la competición, que señalan al Barcelona como el peor de los 20 equipos en un aspecto tan relevante como el rebote. Los azulgranas han capturado 118 rebotes (29,5 de media), a años luz del Estrella Roja, líder en esa faceta con 174 (43,5) o el Valencia, segundo con 162 (40,5). Su endeblez bajo tableros también se refleja en los rebotes defensivos, siendo el cuarto que menos captura (9,8) y el que menos coge bajo su aro con 19,8 de media. La ausencia de Josh Nebo por lesión en tres de los cuatro partidos puede explica en parte esa grieta de su juego que debe sellar cuanto antes para mejorar su eficacia y no dar tantas facilidades a sus rivales. Y el otro gran lunar de los azulgranas en este inicio de campaña europea, tan trascendente como puede ser el del rebote, es el de las asistencias. El Barcelona es el equipo de la Euroliga que menos pases de canasta ha dado hasta ahora, con 56 (14 por partido), muy lejos de los líderes en ese apartado, el ASVEL con 89 (22,3) y el Baskonia con 88 (22). Esa insuficiencia denota, entre otras cosas, que los jugadores aún no se conocen los suficientemente para generar los automatismos que señalábamos anteriormente, y la falta de paciencia para resolver ataques espesos, optando cada uno por buscar la acción individual como solución en lugar de mover el balón hasta encontrar al compañero mejor colocado. No se prodigan los azulgranas en los famosos pases extra y cuando entran las prisas en ataque cada uno va a lo suyo. Les urge subsanar esa desconexión. Ese exceso de individualismo en el que peca en muchas fases de los partidos, con demasiados jugones intentando acaparar protagonismo, puede tener mucho que ver en que sea el equipo que menos balones pierde de toda la Euroliga con 39 (9,8 de media). Muchos tiros y pocos pases por lo que la posibilidad de intercepción de los rivales es mucho menor. Y otro sato que le sitúa en último lugar de la competición es el de las faltas personales. Los de Sekulic son los que menos reciben con 75 (18,8). Tampoco eso ayuda a consolidar su juego, sobre todo en los malos momentos.

articles.title: La asignatura pendiente que saca de quicio al Real Madrid y al madridismo
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, que aún no se han estrenado a domicilio, visitan al colista Milán, donde ha perdido los últimos tres años
articles.summary: Los blancos, que aún no se han estrenado a domicilio, visitan al colista Milán, donde ha perdido los últimos tres años
articles.body: En la temporada pasada, de los 10 equipos que jugaron la postemporada, tanto los Playoffs como el Play-In, el Real Madrid era el equipo con peor balance fuera de casa (6-13). De hecho, en la Liga regular, tardó cinco partidos en lograr su primer triunfo lejos del Movistar Arena. Lo hizo en la jornada 9 en el Palau Blaugrana. La poco fiabilidad del Madrid como visitante llenó de dudas su temporada. Y precisamente los blancos quieren evitar otra situación así. De momento transitan en la Euroliga con un 0-3 fuera de casa. Estrenaron su casillero de victorias la semana pasada ante el Partizan, mochila fuera, pero ahora les queda otra. La de ganar sin el amparo de su afición. La visita de los de Pedro Martínez a Milán puede parecer propicia porque el Armani es el colista de la Euroliga con 1-3, pero en las últimas temporadas el Unipol Forum no ha sido un pabellón fácil para el Madrid. De hecho lleva tres derrotas consecutivas en las últimas tres visitas, un dato que puede poner nervioso a un equipo al que le cuesta sacar los partidos lejos de su público. Además, antes de emprender viaje a Milán el Madrid se llevó en el equipaje la dura lesión de Gabi Deck que será operado en el hombro izquierdo y se estima que cause baja entre cinco o seis meses. Ante el Armani no iba a jugar, pero la lesión que en un principio le iba a tener dos partidos fuera se ha convertido en una ausencia de medio año. En la previa, Pedro Martínez habló del choque de hoy en Italia: “Es un equipo que tiene muchísima variabilidad táctica en su defensa, hacen muchísimas cosas diferentes. Tenemos que estar leyendo y adaptándonos a todas las cosas que van a ir haciendo”, decía el técnico catalán del Madrid, que luego añadió:“Hemos de ser fieles a los valores que entrenamos y a la identidad que queremos tener. articles.title: Michael Jordan jersey from 'Last Dance' season sells for record £10.6m
articles.summary: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
articles.body:
A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season has sold for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.

Jordan wore the Chicago Bulls jersey during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals and has autographed it too.

He scored a game-high 37 points that evening before ending his last season with the Bulls with a 4-2 series win for his sixth and final NBA Championship. He was named the Finals' Most Valuable Player in all six.

The only item of sports memorabilia that has cost more is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he "called the shot" during the 1932 World Series, which was sold for $24.1m (£18.2m) in 2024.

The previous high for a basketball item was a card featuring Jordan and Kobe Bryant from 2007-08 which sold for $12.9m (£9.8m) last year.

The previous record for a piece of game-worn Jordan memorabilia was set just two weeks ago when his jersey from game three of the 1998 Finals, which is not autographed, sold via auction for $12.3m (£9.3m).

The latest purchase was made by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale through Hunt Auctions.

David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement: "While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art."

articles.title: Ranking NBA teams ABA-style uniforms in honor of the 50th anniversary of the historic merger
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets, Denver Nuggets, Indiana Pacers, and San Antonio Spurs unveiled ABA throwback uniforms celebrating the 50th anniversary of the merger.
articles.body: On Monday, four NBA teams unveiled ABA-style uniforms for the upcoming season. The Brooklyn Nets, Denver Nuggets, Indiana Pacers and San Antonio Spurs unveiled new Classic Edition uniforms to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the 1976 NBA-ABA (American Basketball Association) merger. That calls for some uniform rankings. Honorable Mention: San Antonio Spurs These are clean and classic. The Spurs uniforms are a direct reproduction of the team's original home look from their early years in San Antonio. One interesting detail is the arched "Spurs" wordmark on the chest exactly as it was worn by the first players to ever represent the city in 1973 after relocating from Dallas. Jordan Mandelkorn, Vice President of Marketing, Creative and Retail for Spurs Sports & Entertainment, stated that honoring their ABA roots through this uniform provides a unique opportunity to celebrate the history that shaped both the Spurs and the city of San Antonio. He emphasized that the season-long celebration—which includes a matching throwback court design featuring the ABA 50th-anniversary logo—will successfully connect generations of fans to the franchise's past while carrying that legacy into the future. This look was originally made famous during the legendary George Gervin era at the downtown HemisFair Arena. The team has scheduled the jersey to debut on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, against the Dallas Mavericks at the Frost Bank Center, kicking off the first of nine scheduled "Classic Nights" throughout the season. Also, the shorts may be the best of the bunch. The black diamond backdrop framing the classic cowboy spur really nails the retro look. I'm a big fan. The Worst: Denver Nuggets These just don't pass the vibe check. The Nuggets city edition uniforms this season swap out the franchise’s traditional navy and gold for a drab orange design. articles.title: Atlanta Dream hosting WNBA Finals at smaller home arena is an inexcusable, avoidable outcome for league's marquee event
articles.summary: Holding games at Gateway is a disgrace, for both the Dream and the league, and overall a bad idea.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream games at Gateway Center Arena are often described in a similar way, one that president and chief operating officer Morgan Shaw Parker used again last week.

"I can't really describe it," she said. "It's like passing a plate of food with your family and your friends in the backyard. There's also an amazing concert going on, and holy cow, the basketball is insane."

The Dream have proudly touted sellouts of said party for three consecutive seasons. But it's a misnomer, a positive public-relations twist few probe too deeply. Because not all sellouts are built the same, and that fact is about to smack everyone in the face at the worst possible time.

It is looking more and more likely the Dream will hold WNBA Finals games at their 3,500-seat arena in College Park , rather than move them into a larger location. Meanwhile, the rest of the series will take place at Chase Center, where the Golden State Valkyries have sold out every game of their existence with a league-best average attendance of 18,064.

It's intimate versus intimidating. The Atlanta swing of the Finals is about to be mostly friends and family only. No plus-ones allowed. Maybe that works at a Traitors-style dinner party. It doesn't in the WNBA Finals amid an era defined by massive attendance numbers and viewership marks jumping off the bench for a growing league.

Holding games at Gateway is a disgrace, for both the Dream and the league, and overall a bad idea.

Surely, the Dream head honchos aren't all that happy about it, either. They need to grow and support a fan base ahead of moving into State Farm Arena full-time beginning in 2027. Though Shaw Parker said all games, including playoffs, will be held there in the multi-year agreement, the Dream's official press release specified only the 25 regular-season games.

They will miss out on massive championship-level ticket revenue, suite sales and merchandise money from having more people in the arena. Even the tickets they can sell won't equal 3,500. Players will receive comp tickets, and the large media contingent — including broadcast TV partners — covering the Finals will need a place to go. The arena is one level, with limited bar-style seating up top. One basket is courtside seating only.

Shaw Parker said last week every game at State Farm Arena, where they hosted the first round and semifinals, will be a learning opportunity "for what this market will bear" in terms of ticket price points.

But that experiment never received its best test. Nor will a Finals berth help fill out a base that will continue to come to games in downtown Atlanta next year. They always used to say, come to one game and you'll see how exciting it is. You'll want to come back.

Atlanta is missing that chance, despite employing one of the most well-known young talents in the game and building a roster they knew could be in this position.

It's in some ways a kerfuffle of their own making. The Dream used to play in State Farm Arena when it was named Philips Arena, from its inception as an expansion team in 2008 through 2016. The latter 2010s were a tough time for the WNBA, and many teams downsized. The Washington Mystics play at CareFirst Arena, which seats about 4,200. The Aces are a middle child, playing in the 12,000-capacity Michelob Ultra Arena. Most others are in NBA arenas as partners of the local NBA team.

Here's where the Dream find themselves in the bind that's going to cost them. They can't come to a simple agreement to fix this since, as one of the few independent WNBA franchises, Atlanta has no partnership or overlap with State Farm Arena or the main tenant, the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. They individually leased the arena for games they believed could make it worth the deal and did not conflict with other events.

Five games this year were sellouts of 17,044; two against Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever, two against the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces and another against the Chicago Sky, Reese's former team. The sixth, against the Toronto Tempo in June, listed a total attendance of 9,685.

The Dream were able to move the first-round and semifinal dates to State Farm Arena without overlapping the Hawks. The Dream only sold tickets in the lower bowl and listed attendance at around 9,600 in each of the three games, which were labeled as sellouts.

A Sombr concert is scheduled for Oct. 22, the day of Game 3. The Hawks host Houston on Oct. 24, the day of Game 4, in their regular-season home opener, and host Cleveland on Oct. 29, the day of Game 6, in the third game of the home schedule. The Hawks averaged 16,355 fans per game in 2025-26, and started strong with a sold-out 17,811 at their home opener.

It does not behoove either party to upend their own highly intricate logistics to bend around the Dream when they aren't partners in either ownership or arena tenants. This isn't a charity wherein people are loud enough on social media to disrupt those with better planning and awareness. The Valkyries could boot Doja Cat to a contingency date because they are under the NBA's Warriors' ownership group, and they own Chase Arena.

The WNBA Finals schedule went out to teams in December, and the Dream set themselves up to make it to the end. They traded for Reese as their missing piece in April, as soon as they could following the delayed collective bargaining agreement (CBA), and signed DeWanna Bonner on Aug. 27 after the veteran agreed to a buyout with the Phoenix Mercury.

It is unclear how long the Dream have been in discussions with State Farm on the use of their arena, or with other locations around the city. The only correct answer is since January. Anything else is a dereliction of duty for a franchise attempting to become one of the best in the league and solidify itself in a crowded Atlanta space.

It's understandable they want to keep things the same for the players instead of moving elsewhere, as they seek the first WNBA championship in franchise history. They were swept in all three Finals they reached in 2010, 2011 and 2013.

To win is not only meaningful for the players individually, but the franchise collectively as it continues down its five- and 10-year plan. Arguably, it's ahead of schedule. Yet again, it could fall back behind by keeping potential fans away from seeing its home team clinch a historic championship.

The Dream touted all week how they built it. It's looking more and more like they won't be able to see if the people will come.

articles.title: Why Roddy Gayle Jr. didn't play in Michigan basketball exhibition
articles.summary: Roddy Gayle Jr. was in Ann Arbor, but didn't play in a Michigan basketball exhibition win over EMU. Coach Mike Boynton Jr. explained why Monday.
articles.body:
After an offseason of wondering if Roddy Gayle Jr. had another season of Michigan basketball eligibility, he was on hand for the Wolverines' 87-62 exhibition win over Eastern Michigan.

Just one problem, though: He never took off his warmup outfit, spending his entire afternoon on Sunday, Oct. 11, on the Crisler Center bench. The reason? Some suspect wording on last month's New York court ruling ostensibly giving him a fifth year of NCAA participation.

"All this stuff is fairly nuanced," coach Mike Boynton Jr. said while explaining why Kenny Noland, a transfer from Columbia who also won a fifth year through the courts, was cleared to play but Gayle was not. "His injunction order didn't address his participation in [NBA] Summer League. Simple as that.

"There needs to be an amendment added to the injunction that says, 'This includes not having anything to do with his participation in Summer League,' which we hope will be in the next couple days."

The hope for Gayle, who spent a couple weeks on the Detroit Pistons' Las Vegas Summer League squad but did not sign an Exhibit 10 contract, is to be able to play in U-M's next exhibition, against Oregon State (led by former Michigan assistant Justin Joyner) on Friday (7 p.m., B1G+).

Gayle is one of dozens of players across the country who took the NCAA to court to gain eligibility under its adopted-in-June "five-in-five" rule, which states players may play five years of college athletics beginning immediately after high school or they turn 19, whichever comes first.

Still, even without court time, Gayle has been a vocal leader during practice and a stabilizing force on the bench, according to teammate J.P. Estrella.

"It's great having that veteran leader back," the Tennessee transfer said after he scored 14 points Sunday. "He's a guy that made a huge impact last year, and he's already making a huge impact already this year in practice. Just talking, just telling us little things, even on the bench today in the huddles.

"He really has a big voice in this group, which is super beneficial because we need that out of him − just his overall game is really good. I mean, we're gonna be really good if we get him [back and] get this thing rolling."

Gayle played in 39 of U-M's 40 games last season, averaging 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 21.1 minutes per game. He played in 146 games across his career, starting 72 games (including 25 for U-M in 2025-26).

Michigan is thin on the wing after freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. was lost for the season to an ACL injury. Without the McDonald's All-American or Gayle, the Wolverines would be relying on a combination of Ricky Liburd (who redshirted last year), Oscar Goodman (who more naturally fits as a four) and freshmen Quinn Costello, Malachi Brown and Joseph Hartmann.

Even with the uncertainty, Michigan is working as though it will have Gayle for a third season in Ann Arbor (after he spent his first two years with Ohio State).

"There's a there's an aspect of of this that's new for everybody, right?," Boynton said last week at the Big Ten's basketball media days. "This is sort of uncharted territory. Right now, he's eligible. We're functioning as if he's eligible. ... We feel like he's got a strong case. We're excited about the opportunity and the things that he adds to our team, and we look forward to moving forward with the information we have in front of us."

Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia .

articles.title: “They can adjust” – Linda Cohn Raises Eyebrows Over Atlanta Dream’s Comfort-First Approach To Finals Venue Decision
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries are set to battle for the 2026 WNBA title. Angel Reese is debuting in the finals, and fans have high anticip...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries are set to battle for the 2026 WNBA title. Angel Reese is debuting in the finals, and fans have high anticipation for the event. However, the team decided to hold the series in a smaller venue, which is their usual home arena, so the team feels comfortable in the finals.

The home-court advantage belongs to the higher seed, so the Valkyries will host most of the seven-game series.

Meanwhile, the Dream has reportedly decided to play at the Gateway Center Arena in College Park, which holds just 3,500 fans, although management has other options, like Georgia Tech basketball's home stadium, McCamish Pavilion; Gas South Arena in Duluth; and others. State Farm Arena, where the team occasionally plays, has a capacity of 17 thousand fans, but is unavailable.

Sports analyst Linda Cohn called out the team's reluctance to play at a bigger arena on X on Monday:

"These are professional basketball players. They can adjust. Wouldn't they want to play in a venue larger than a high school gym so their fans can actually attend and the league can grow?"

The Dream's usage of State Farm Arena was under scrutiny for accommodating only a smaller audience for WNBA postseason games (not selling the upper deck seats).

The Dream and the Valkyries have a weeklong break before the finals, which will be a boon for someone like Allisha Gray, who has been out of the lineup due to a finger injury.

The Dream won't play at State Farm Arena as it's pre-booked

State Farm Arena, which is the home arena of the Atlanta Hawks of the NBA, was also one of the team's options for the WNBA Finals. However, the venue is reportedly booked for a Shane Michael Boose, aka Sombr, concert on Oct. 22 and for the Hawks' regular-season games on Oct. 24 and 29.

Atlanta is in the finals for the first time since 2013 and has a real chance at the title, considering Gray is available for the final series. DeWanna Bonner has contributed well to the frontcourt, alongside Reese and Rhyne Howard, who will be crucial against the Valkyries.

articles.title: Mavs 'Believe In' Kyrie Irving, Masai Ujiri Says amid Latest NBA Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Kyrie Irving found his name in trade rumors over the offseason, but Dallas Mavericks president Masai Ujiri made it clear that the team values their veteran point guard.
articles.body:
Kyrie Irving found his name in trade rumors over the offseason, but Dallas Mavericks president Masai Ujiri made it clear that the team values their veteran point guard.

Ujiri said the Mavs "truly believe in" Irving on the Hoop Collective podcast.

"Kyrie, as a player, we truly believe in him. We truly believe that he can succeed on our team," Ujiri said (15:20 mark). "I truly believe that, if we have the right players playing, we can really grow as a team in a new system with Dusty (May) and a new culture that we're trying to build."

Several teams, including the Detroit Pistons, reportedly have interest in trading for Irving, but the Mavs may be interested in keeping him around to help as they enter a new era under head coach Dusty May.

The 34-year-old Irving missed all of the 2025-26 campaign because of a torn ACL, but he was highly productive in his last healthy season, putting up 24.7 points, 4.8 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game.

Dallas perhaps isn't expecting to compete for a championship this year, but it should be in for a year of growth as Cooper Flagg progresses and May settles in as head coach.

Having a veteran player with championship experience like Irving can certainly help expedite a rebuild.

articles.title: WNBA gives Cheryl Reeve another award after playoff collapse and years of outspoken left-wing politics
articles.summary: Cheryl Reeve won WNBA Executive of the Year for a third time, but the Lynx's historic first-round playoff sweep raises questions about the honor.
articles.body: The WNBA has another award for Cheryl Reeve. This one comes from the people who run the teams, and that makes it worth examining what, exactly, they are celebrating. The league announced Monday that the Minnesota Lynx head coach and president of basketball operations won Basketball Executive of the Year for the third time, tying the Atlanta Dream's Dan Padover for the most selections in the award's history. The announcement comes less than two weeks after the top-seeded Lynx were swept out of the first round of the playoffs by the eighth-seeded New York Liberty, who were subsequently swept in the semifinals by the Dream. Reeve appeared on 13 ballots, ahead of Padover's 11 and Golden State's Ohemaa Nyanin's eight. Each of the WNBA's 15 teams had an executive on the voting panel, and voters couldn't select themselves. CHERYL REEVE'S WNBA COACH OF THE YEAR WIN SHOULDN'T DISTRACT FROM HER DANGEROUS ACCUSATIONS That's a substantial endorsement of Reeve from her peers and it also amounts to tacit approval of the way one of the league's most outspoken left-wing figures represents her franchise. An executive helps establish what an organization stands for, and Reeve has made her politics a major part of that job. She consistently uses her WNBA platform to attack the motives of people who believe women's sports should be reserved for females. Her colleagues have now chosen to celebrate her leadership. That deserves scrutiny beyond a list of successful transactions. Dallas made Reeve's Olivia Miles decision awfully easy The league's announcement highlighted Reeve's selection of Olivia Miles with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. Miles went on to become the unanimous Rookie of the Year and set the league's rookie scoring record with 790 points. An excellent addition, obviously. But let's remember how Miles became available. The Dallas Wings could have (and should have) taken Miles, but elected to draft Paige Bueckers' girlfriend, Azzi Fudd, with the No. 1 pick instead. The Wings publicly praised Fudd's shooting. But pretending that their selection of Fudd was based entirely on her basketball skills is foolish. Miles averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds as a rookie. Fudd averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists and 1.7 rebounds. Miles produced those numbers while playing slightly fewer minutes per game, shot better from the field and finished second in MVP voting. Reeve should probably send the Wings a thank-you note. In April 2024, the Chicago Sky moved from No. 8 to No. 7 and acquired the rights to Nikolina Milić. Minnesota received Sika Koné, a 2025 second-round pick and the right to swap first-round picks with Chicago in 2026, along with the No. 8 selection. Chicago used No. 7 on Angel Reese. At the time of the deal, Minnesota was coming off a 19-21 season and Chicago an 18-22 season. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND In April 2025, Minnesota sent Chicago the No. 11 pick, which the Sky used on Hailey Van Lith, for Chicago's 2026 first-rounder outright. That deal canceled the earlier swap and allowed Minnesota to keep its own 2026 first-round pick, too. Reeve deserves credit for those trades. Once Dallas passed on Miles, though, the choice at No. 2 was awfully easy. Reeve also signed Natasha Howard, who started all 44 games and earned an All-Star starting spot. Minnesota finished 33-11 and earned the No. 1 playoff seed. Dallas did Reeve an enormous favor, and the Lynx benefited. Reeve's team couldn't win a playoff game For all those advantages, what did the Lynx do in the playoffs? Minnesota became the first No. 1 seed in WNBA history to be eliminated by a No. 8 seed, and New York did it in a sweep. The Lynx had the unanimous Rookie of the Year (who also finished second in MVP voting). And while Napheesa Collier, one of the league’s best players, missed time during the regular season, she played in both playoff games. Minnesota lost both of those games by 16 points, including a 91-75 defeat at home in Game 1. Reeve's four championships are part of her record. So is the fact that the most recent one came in 2017. In the nine seasons since, Minnesota has reached the Finals once, losing to New York in 2024. During that same stretch, Reeve has collected three Coach of the Year awards and all three of her Executive of the Year awards. Six individual awards. Zero championships. If Reeve gets the credit for both building the roster and coaching it, she can answer for what that team did in the playoffs, too. An executive sets the tone for the franchise Reeve already won her fifth Coach of the Year award two weeks ago. With Monday's announcement, she became the first person to win Coach of the Year and Executive of the Year in the same season twice. For me, evaluating an executive means evaluating leadership. If an executive repeatedly uses the team's platform to make political statements, those statements belong in the discussion of how she represents the organization. WNBA FIGHT OVER MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS EXPOSES HOW THE LEFT KEEPS ANSWERING A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt on the sideline against the Indiana Fever shortly after Sophie Cunningham's comments about wanting to protect women's sports went public. But she wasn't done. After Minnesota's Sept. 24 regular-season finale, Reeve characterized the controversy involving male participation in women's sports as an attack on what she called the "transgender community." "They don't want transgender people to exist," Reeve said. That's an ugly accusation to make about people whose position is that girls and women deserve their own athletic category. And it came from the person who both coaches the Lynx and oversees their basketball operations. Her public conduct carries the authority of both positions. By honoring Reeve as the year's outstanding basketball executive, her peers are publicly holding up her leadership as an example. Her political conduct is part of that leadership. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The same people entrusted with running women's basketball teams are applauding a leader who talks openly about allowing males to compete in women's sports and share their locker rooms. That says a lot about what the WNBA's decision-makers will celebrate.

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa, Trae Young's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Nets vs. Wizards Preseason
articles.summary: The top pick in the 2026 NBA draft is just over a week away from making his rookie debut, and he's continuing to impress in preseason ahead of his first game.
articles.body:
The top pick in the 2026 NBA draft is just over a week away from making his rookie debut, and he's continuing to impress in preseason ahead of his first game.

AJ Dybantsa and the Washington Wizards lost to the Brooklyn Nets, 131-122, in their penultimate preseason game on Monday. Dybantsa had a slow start to the night but got things going late to finish with a solid stat line.

Trae Young, who is eyeing a big first full season with the Wizards, posted a double-double in the loss as the Wizards were without Anthony Davis.

Dybantsa posted 11 points in his preseason debut last week before putting up 14 against the Detroit Pistons. The former BYU star led the nation in scoring last year, but he'll need some time to adjust to NBA defenses before he starts lighting up the box score in the league.

Still, consistently reaching double figures this early in his career is a good sign for a player facing NBA-level talent for the first time.

The Wizards likely won't be contenders this year, but it wouldn't be surprising if they snuck into the playoffs. With veterans Young and Davis and lots of young talent, highlighted by Dybantsa, Washington managed to expedite its rebuild.

The Wizards have their final preseason game on Friday against the New Orleans Pelicans and will tip off the regular season on Oct. 21 against the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: Michael Jordan’s ‘Last Dance’ NBA Finals jersey sells for record $14m
articles.summary: The basketball memorabilia ranks as the second-largest sale in history ⁠⁠among game-worn sports jerseys.
articles.body:
The jersey Michael Jordan wore during ‌‌Game 2 of the “Last Dance” 1998 NBA Finals has sold for a ⁠⁠record $14m.

Hunt Auctions ⁠⁠announced on Monday that the game-worn, autographed Chicago Bulls jersey was bought by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale.

It is the highest ⁠⁠price ever paid for a piece of basketball memorabilia and, according to the auction house, the newly sold Jordan jersey ranks as the second-largest sale in history ⁠⁠among game-worn sports jerseys.

The New York Yankees jersey worn by Babe Ruth in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series – during which Ruth called his shot before a home run – went for $24.12m in 2024.

Jordan and the Bulls defeated the Utah Jazz in ‌‌six games to win the 1998 championship, the sixth and final title of his career in Chicago.

Game 2, played on June 5, 1998, in Salt Lake City, saw Chicago even the series 1-1, largely thanks to a dominant performance by its superstar guard.

Jordan put up 37 points, five rebounds, and three assists in a 93-88 victory. He would go on to collect his sixth ⁠⁠and final Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP) award, two more than anyone ⁠⁠else in NBA history, nine days later.

The wildly popular “Last Dance” documentary, released in 2020, was centred around that 1997-98 Bulls season.

“The record-setting price achieved for the related Michael Jordan jersey is yet another corroborative result as ⁠⁠to the significance of Jordan within the industry and popular culture. This remarkable garment bore witness to one of Jordan’s most ⁠⁠hallowed NBA Finals appearances as part of his ‘Last ⁠⁠Dance’ season to complete his illustrious career,” David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement.

“While Michael Jordan’s importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite ‌‌asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art. We are very pleased to have been able to facilitate this historic sale which serves as another benchmark for our ‌‌industry.”

This sale becomes at least the third time a Jordan jersey from that 1998 Finals has fetched at least $10m. A jersey from Game 1 was sold at auction for about $10.1m in 2022, and a jersey from Game 3 was auctioned last month for about $12.3m via an auction in September.

“Michael Jordan was an incredibly talented player who is admired around the world,” Firman said in a news release distributed by the auction house. “I’m very excited about the purchase.”

The jersey that Firman bought was originally bought from the Bulls by a private collector in 2003, Hunt said, adding that it “has remained within a succinct chain of custody, having only changed hands once from the original purchaser”.

Just about anything related to the 1998 Finals and Jordan’s final season with the Bulls has been the subject of huge interest in the collector space. In 2023, a pair of Air Jordan sneakers that he wore in Game 2 against the Jazz was sold by Sotheby’s for $2.2m, touted at the time as “a new world record for the most valuable sneakers ever sold”.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball Praised by Timberwolves Coach Chris Finch
articles.summary: Newly acquired Minnesota Timberwolves point guard LaMelo Ball was praised by his new head coach, Chris Finch, ahead of the upcoming season.The Timberwolves s...
articles.body:
Newly acquired Minnesota Timberwolves point guard LaMelo Ball was praised by his new head coach, Chris Finch, ahead of the upcoming season.

The Timberwolves sent big man Naz Reid and a package of draft picks to the Charlotte Hornets for Ball, who is getting a fresh start in Minnesota, a perennial playoff contender, after many years without playing in the postseason in Charlotte.

Although the season has not started yet, Finch has loved what he's seen from Ball during practice and in preseason games, and he's excited about what the team will look like this coming season with Ball and NBA superstar Anthony Edwards playing alongside each other in Minnesota.

Chris Finch Has High Praise for LaMelo Ball

Speaking to reporters during the preseason, Finch had nothing but high praise for Ball, suggesting that his giddy personality will be a great fit in Minnesota's locker room and on the court.

"He's always in a great mood. Always comes in smiling. He and Anthony have a shared quality: they're really hard to stay mad at. And they do some things that you want to get mad at. They have a reflective joy…We referred to ourselves as a moody team in the last couple of years, at times, and it's probably gotten in our way. We've traded moodiness for giddiness. So, we've gotta get to some sort of happy medium," Finch said.

The Timberwolves made several lineup changes during the offseason to change up their makeup for this coming season.

The big move was, of course, trading away Reid and getting Ball in return . But the team also signed free-agent forward Jonathan Kuminga, whom they believe has untapped potential that the Timberwolves believe he can reach in Minnesota.

Combine those newcomers with Edwards plus other holdovers in Rudy Gobert and Jaden McDaniels, and the Timberwolves will likely be among the top contenders in the NBA's Western Conference once again.

There are a lot of great teams on paper in the league this year, but Minnesota hopes that when springtime comes around next year, they'll be among the final teams remaining.

articles.title: ‘Either Way the League Loses’ — ESPN Legend Laments ‘Sad’ State of WNBA Finals As Arena Controversy Overshadows Angel Reese, Dream
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream are heading to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013, but their historic run has been overshadowed by a major arena problem. ESPN l...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are heading to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013, but their historic run has been overshadowed by a major arena problem.

ESPN legend Linda Cohn has called the situation a "sad" reflection of the league, as questions grow about why Angel Reese and her teammates may have to play championship games in a venue with just 3,500 seats.

Linda Cohn Claims Angel Reese, Dream Playing WNBA Finals in 3,500-Seat Arena Would Be an 'Embarrassment'

The Dream usually play most of their home games at Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Georgia. The venue holds around 3,500 fans for basketball, making it the WNBA's smallest arena.

However, Atlanta has also played selected games at State Farm Arena, home of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. The venue holds more than 17,000 people and hosted the Dream's three home playoff games this year, which drew an average of almost 9,700 fans.

The team hoped to use State Farm Arena for the Finals, but scheduling conflicts have hindered that plan. A concert is scheduled there on Oct. 22, while Hawks games are booked for Oct. 24 and 29. Those dates coincide with Games 3 and 4 of the Finals and Game 6, if needed.

The Dream's home venue for the 2026 WNBA Finals remains unconfirmed, with reports indicating Gateway Center is the likely option.

Cohn, a former longtime ESPN anchor, believes the controversy has put the WNBA in a lose-lose situation, with the league receiving negative publicity instead of attention for basketball.

If the Dream play their home Finals games in a 3,500-seat arena, it could call into question the WNBA's growth at a time when it wants to attract more fans. But if a larger venue is announced at the last minute, the league could still face criticism for taking so long to find one.

"I can't help wondering whether the controversy is giving the Finals publicity they otherwise wouldn't be getting, and that's a pretty sad commentary, isn't it?" Cohn said on Monday's episode of "The Linda Cohn Show."

"Because either way, I think the league loses. Either way, they lose."

Cohn added that playing in a 3,500-seat arena would be an "embarrassment" for a league trying to show its growth.

Fans have also voiced frustration online, with some calling the situation "horrendous" and demanding that the games be moved.

When it comes to the Finals, the stakes are significant. Atlanta swept the New York Liberty in the semifinals to reach its first Finals in 13 years, while the other finalists, the Golden State Valkyries, swept the defending champion Las Vegas Aces. The matchup guarantees a first WNBA championship for one of the franchises.

Reese has been central to Atlanta's run, but instead of the Finals being defined by Reese and Atlanta's title bid, the arena dispute has become the major talking point.

articles.title: Angel Reese is leading Caitlin Clark in the only thing that matters: Winning rings
articles.summary: Angel Reese was working her last college handshake line when she stopped briefly to whisper something in Caitlin Clark's right ear. "Keep elevating the game...
articles.body:
Angel Reese was working her last college handshake line when she stopped briefly to whisper something in Caitlin Clark's right ear.

"Keep elevating the game and go win it," Reese told her rival after Iowa beat the defending champ, Louisiana State, in the NCAA Tournament's Elite Eight.

Clark did not win it in 2024, falling to South Carolina in the final, one year after falling to LSU in the final. To punctuate that Tigers triumph, Reese famously taunted her Iowa counterpart by mimicking John Cena's "You can't see me" gesture — Clark did it less conspicuously against Louisville a week earlier — and by pointing to her soon-to-be-sparkling ring finger.

Whatever you thought of Reese's on-court celebration, this much is true:

In big-time college and professional sports, the ring is the thing. You either win one or you don't.

Clark has made it clear where winning a title stands among her priorities with the Indiana Fever. "That's my main goal," she said in her recent season wrap of a news conference. Clark added that she plans to have a voice in the Fever's offseason moves, and that she will weigh her eligibility for a big raise under the EPIC (exceptional performance on initial contract) extension against the team's needs while building a contender under the salary cap.

"I just think for myself," Clark said, "it's more a decision of how we can best construct a roster and what's going to be best for our team to help us win championships."

Clark knows how the superstar game is played. She knows that even in a team sport, first-round playoff losses are permanently attached to a franchise player's legacy … unless there are ring ceremonies to come.

And in that context, Reese has a chance to take a commanding lead in the only race with Clark that really matters. Starting Saturday, her Atlanta Dream face the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals. If the Dream prevail, Reese will have a pro ring to go with her college ring — along with the FIBA World Cup gold medal she won with Clark in September.

That's a big deal, too, at a time when WNBA players feel that so much in their universe is out of their control. Most unfortunately, they can't control the hateful social media messages sent their way. They can't control the TV ratings and attendance figures that tilt heavily toward one special third-year guard over more established and decorated veterans (through no fault of Clark's).

They can't control who league marketing experts and Madison Avenue executives choose as the face of the sport and the centerpiece of a clever State Farm ad campaign (again, through no fault of Clark's).

But they can control who wins and loses between the lines, and that will never change. Clark's Fever were swept by the Connecticut Sun in two first-round games in 2024 and were eliminated by A'ja Wilson, now a five-time MVP, and her Las Vegas Aces in three first-round games this year. In between, an injured Clark missed Indiana's first-round victory over Atlanta and five-game loss to Las Vegas in the semis in 2025.

Reese was liberated from a dire situation in Chicago — the Sky were 23-61 in her first two WNBA seasons — and gifted an ideal alternative in Atlanta. With the Dream, she led the league in rebounding for a third straight year, contributing to a 30-14 regular season that gave way to a five-game playoff winning streak and a spot in the finals. In the last two games of the Dream's three-game sweep of the New York Liberty, Reese delivered a combined 45 points, 16 rebounds and four blocks.

After that series, Dream coach Karl Smesko spoke of his plan to make a deep playoff run. "Then we added the perfect piece to really bring that plan to life," he said. "And Angel has been everything we could have hoped for."

Reese is very much her own person, her own force of talent and will, and it's fair to ask why her accomplishments need to be measured against Clark's in the first place. In a 2024 CNBC interview made infamous by her failure to appropriately respond to the racism and homophobia that players face online, now-outgoing commissioner Cathy Engelbert called the arrival of Clark and Reese "a little of that Bird-Magic moment if you recall from 1979, when those two rookies came in from a big college rivalry, one White, one Black."

Larry Bird and Magic Johnson hated that race was an everyday part of their shared NBA journey, but they acknowledged it as fact. Not that race is at all a necessary component of an intense rivalry shaped by sweeping differences in style, appearance, personality and approach. Ali-Frazier. Palmer-Nicklaus. Evert-Navratilova. Russell-Chamberlain. And on and on.

But however they are defined, rivalries are essential for box-office appeal. The 1979 NCAA final between Magic's Michigan State and Bird's Indiana State put the madness in March before the blood feud between Magic's Los Angeles Lakers and Bird's Boston Celtics helped transform the NBA from a second-rate circuit into a global juggernaut.

Magic and Bird were admittedly jealous of each other, at least until they shot a Converse commercial in 1985 in Bird's hometown, French Lick, Ind., and ate lunch at the Bird home (Bird's mother told Johnson he was her favorite player) and realized they had so much in common. In a world without social media, they could become good friends off the court while remaining bitter enemies on it, a fact that inspired David Letterman to ask Bird this question while both men were on his late-night show in 2012:

"Do you now in your heart believe you're the better player?"

"Actually," Bird replied, "I've always said that I go by success and he's won more championships. So I give him the nod."

Including the NCAA clash, Johnson had Bird by a ring count of 6-3, including 3-1 head-to-head. Hey, it's the only way legends know how to keep score at home.

Let's face it, if Clark and Reese ever meet with a WNBA championship on the line, it will be a fever dream of a Fever-Dream spectacle. Talk about a show; those TV ratings might even make the NFL sweat. That Bird-Magic moment Engelbert referenced would be at hand.

It's good news that, from the outside looking in, Clark and Reese appear headed toward the kind of long-term kinship that Magic and Bird enjoy today, a relationship that will help Team USA in future international events. At the World Cup in Berlin, Clark shot down a reporter who brought up Reese and asked if they were "friends now," suggesting they weren't friends before.

After their 2024 Elite Eight matchup won by Clark, the two stars encouraged each other to keep chasing greatness in their quick handshake exchange. Now Reese stands four victories away from catching it on a higher level.

They are both too skilled and too competitive not to win multiple WNBA titles before their careers are done. But just in case, Angel Reese has a golden opportunity here to get out in front and try to stay there for keeps.

articles.title: B/R 99: Ranking the 99 Best NBA Players Ahead of 2026-27
articles.summary: Debating top-10-star status has become a rite of passage for NBA fandom.
articles.body:
Debating top-10-star status has become a rite of passage for NBA fandom.

Is Steph Curry still among that elite group at 38? What about Jayson Tatum after his Achilles comeback? Donovan Mitchell after another failure to make the Finals?

But why stop there? Heading into the 2026-27 season, the B/R NBA staff is ready to litigate who's who among the Association's best, from No. 1 through 99. This year, we upped the ante a bit by using a breakdown of five skill categories to arrive at a final overall rating.

As in seasons past, we're not predicting where players will finish in April. This is a breakdown of where the league stands right now. Meaning players set to start the year on the sidelines aren't included. Sorry, Jimmy Butler.

Player summaries and preview content by Andy Bailey. For a full methodology breakdown, scroll to the infographic below.

Category ratings are set up as an intentional bell curve with a median of 75.

Each category counts toward the Full Rating by these shares.

Players also receive ratings bonuses for ranking in the top 10, top 5 or top 3 of multiple categories.

B/R editors reviewed the results to ensure the final rankings reflected informed basketball judgment.

Is Giannis Antetokounmpo Really Not a Top-5 Player?

Our methodology nudged Giannis Antetokounmpo out of the top five, and that might be the biggest reason to call it into question.

Anthony Edwards and Jalen Brunson are phenomenal scorers and guards. They're the faces of teams that have had more playoff success than Giannis in recent years. But in a vacuum, it'd be hard to seriously argue that either is a more effective individual player than Antetokounmpo.

Over the last three seasons, he's averaged more points in fewer minutes than both, has averaged more rebounds than both combined, had a field-goal percentage about 13 percentage points higher than both and has a box plus/minus that's higher than Edwards' and Brunson's combined.

There are plenty of numbers that suggest Stephen Curry shouldn't be in the top 10 anymore. He only played 1,329 minutes last season. And an aggregation of advanced numbers from around the internet suggests he didn't have a top-20 impact in 2025-26.

Thinking things might get better as he enters his age-38 season is bold, but Curry has earned the vote of confidence.

Curry was sixth in the league in points per 75 possessions last season. Among the top 11 in that category, only Giannis, Jokic and SGA had higher true shooting percentages. And even at his advanced age, there still isn't another player who bends a defense without the ball like Curry does.

With anything resembling a contending-level supporting cast, Curry being in the top 10 would probably feel like a no-brainer.

Will LeBron James Finish the Season in the Top 20?

Logic suggests the answer on this one has to be "no."

LeBron is entering his age-42 season. When everyone's available, he may be the fourth option on offense. Some nights, even VJ Edgecombe might command a bigger share of the team's shot diet. And with some of the players currently behind LeBron on this list being on the rise (like Cooper Flagg, Deni Avdija and LaMelo Ball), a dip feels more likely for LeBron.

But we're going on 24 years of LeBron completely breaking expectations. And even if he doesn't shoot as much as he has on previous teams, he could certainly reestablish himself as one of the league's very best playmakers with all the scorers around him in Philadelphia.

So no, he probably won't make his way into the top 20 this season. But it certainly wouldn't be shocking if he did.

How High Can a Healthy Kyrie Irving Rise in Our Rankings?

Coming off a torn ACL and entering his age-34 campaign, Kyrie Irving is outside the top 30 right now. If he struggles with availability, he'll probably stay there.

But as you scan the top 20, names like Devin Booker, Jamal Murray and Jaylen Brown stand out. And if Kyrie can stay healthy, it wouldn't be shocking to see him have a better individual season than any of the above.

Even at his age and with his growing injury history, Irving is one of the most skilled guards and reliable shooters in the NBA. Best-case scenario, he could find himself back in the top 20 before this season ends.

Can the Ja Morant, Damian Lillard Backcourt Prove Us Wrong?

Portland Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori has already tossed some cold water on the idea of Damian Lillard and Ja Morant starting together, noting that both are undersized and historically non-elite defenders.

But with their talent level, it'll be hard to keep the duo separated all the time. And at least on the offensive end, Morant's slashing and Lillard's shooting could be devastatingly complementary. Morant's drives could pull defenses away from the three-point line, creating extra time for Lillard's shots. And at the same time, Lillard's gravity as a shooter could force those same defenses out of the paint, making the driving lanes wider for Morant. The symbiosis isn't hard to imagine.

But yes, it's going to take a Herculean effort from the rest of the rotation on the other end.

articles.title: President Trump Tells Ohio Rally Crowd That WNBA Star Sophie Cunningham Is “A Beautiful Young Woman” and Says Teams Would Want Her “Not To Help You With Points, But To Help You With Attendance”
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump called Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham “beautiful” at a campaign rally on Monday. He joked that teams appreciate the WNBA p...
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump called Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham "beautiful" at a campaign rally on Monday. He joked that teams appreciate the WNBA player for her ability to draw fans rather than score points.

The president was campaigning for Republican candidates before the November 3 midterm elections. Trump explained that many men want to watch Cunningham, adding that one had to be careful praising a woman's appearance politically.

"Hey, you have a lot of men wanting to go and watch her. She's beautiful," Trump said. "You're not allowed to say that anymore, however. As a politician, please, please, let me take it back."

"Anytime a politician says a woman is beautiful, that's generally the end of his political career in the modern-day political world," he added. "But Sophie is a beautiful young woman."

Discussing her potential benefit to a team, the president went on, "You probably wouldn't mind her on the team, not to help you with points, but to help you with attendance. The attendance would be quite good."

His comments drew criticism from those who thought Trump focused on Cunningham's appearance rather than her on-court skills. Nevertheless, others agreed with him because it became clear she drew fans, and she will become a free agent soon.

Last year, Cunningham averaged 7.9 points per game and made 41.9% of three-point shots. She was one of the Fever's main bench players, adding a physical presence alongside their star, Caitlin Clark.

Off the court, she has built a large fan base through her physical style of play and social media presence. Moreover, she has been criticized for opposing transgender athletes playing in the women's sport.

articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors star player, has been a dedicated player to the team ever since he was drafted in the league, close to two decades ago. While the four time NBA champion sustained brutal injuries in the last season, he is now ready to get back to court.
