articles.title: Blake Griffin Reveals 'The Stepback' Trailer, Talks NBA Finals Prediction and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Once known for his rim-rocking slam dunks that seemed to shake the stratosphere, former NBA star Blake Griffin is taking a lighter approach to his media career.
articles.body:
Once known for his rim-rocking slam dunks that seemed to shake the stratosphere, former NBA star Blake Griffin is taking a lighter approach to his media career.

In addition to entering his second season as an analyst for NBA on Prime Video, Griffin is set to host a new weekly late-night television show, The Stepback with Blake Griffin . The trailer for the new series, which is produced by Griffin and Ryan Kalil's Mortal Media in partnership with Wondery, officially dropped on Tuesday morning ahead of its Oct. 20 premiere on Prime Video and YouTube.

Blending late-night-style comedy with insightful commentary, Griffin plans to explore the biggest topics in sports in front of a live studio audience, tackling matters such as the economics of sports betting, athlete empowerment, officiating controversies, the rise of "hot take" culture and more.

"There's a lot of things in sports, I think, that affect fans a lot and affect how we view sports or what's going on in sports. And I wanted to create a show that sort of spoke to fans on bigger issues in sports, not necessarily the day-to-day," Griffin told Bleacher Report. "... I learned a lot making this show. And the research team for this show did such an incredible job, and our writers' room. And I hope [the viewers] learn something, because I definitely did, and also just are entertained, enjoy it along the way."

While The Stepback will dive into some serious topics, Griffin ensured that he plans to bring a light-hearted approach that shows off his comedic range. The 37-year-old's comedy career dates back to his days in Hollywood playing for the Los Angeles Clippers, and he has done stand-up on multiple occasions and has guest-starred on shows like The Eric Andre Show and The Simpsons .

For Griffin, the chance to pursue comedy fulfills a childhood dream that once took a backseat to his basketball career.

"I always go back to when it started for me, and how I really fell in love with comedy was watching comedy shows with my parents. When I was really young, I remember watching I Love Lucy and just thinking like, 'Oh my gosh, this is amazing.' Just the idea that you can be so silly and goofy and make people laugh, it definitely got the wheels turning at a very young age," he said. "And then watching Saturday Night Live as a kid, In Living Color as a kid, and then starting to watch stand-up with my dad, Richard Pryor, Eddie Murphy, all those guys. And as I got older, I started seeking it out on my own, all the way from Chappelle's Show to [Dave] Chappelle's stand-up to everything in between. I've always just kind of gravitated towards comedy."

The 2025-26 NBA season was Griffin's first year as a full-time member of the media. While he admitted that he was initially intimidated by the lights, cameras and action, he quickly learned that authenticity would be the key to success in his new career. Rather than playing the role of a critical analyst, he maintained his jovial nature as he uplifted his former peers in a positive way.

"I think even before the show started, I was kind of in my head a little bit about, 'OK, you gotta have high energy, you gotta be the TV person.' And I never tried to do that. I always tried to be myself," he said. "... It's more about trying to bring perspective to fans in a way that they maybe haven't thought of before, or maybe a way that you're not able to really see if you're just watching the game. And I think that was sort of my biggest lesson: just be authentic and celebrate. I don't need to bring anybody down. This is a very, very tough profession, and there's very few guys who do it really well. And I think celebrating that was a lot of fun for me."

The NBA landscape shifted significantly before Griffin's second season as an analyst, most notably with future Hall of Famer LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers. While other teams made splashy moves like the Miami Heat acquiring star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Minnesota Timberwolves acquiring star point guard LaMelo Ball, the Sixers landing James completed a banner offseason that also included the acquisition of star guard Jaylen Brown.

"That alone puts them in a dangerous category," Griffin said of Brown's arrival to Philadelphia from the Boston Celtics. "And then you add in a guy like LeBron, who has clearly shown he's willing to adapt his game to different styles. I mean, last year when he came back from injury with the Lakers, he was kind of playing a third-option role, which is an incredible luxury to have one of the best players of all time playing in that role. He's so skilled at so many different things that he's really a key piece. If he just finds that role, whatever they need and does that, they will be good."

It will likely take time for James and Brown to develop chemistry with their new teammates, as will the rest of the new faces in new places. However, Griffin wondered more about who would step up after losing the role players who were shipped away to land the stars.

"Honestly, with some of these teams, it's almost like my biggest questions are not necessarily LaMelo going to the Timberwolves, it's Naz Reid not being there, Julius Randle not being there. So it's like, how are we filling these gaps?" he said. "And the Heat, the same thing, they're going to be incredible. It's just, what do you do when you're not having a great shooting night in the playoffs?"

One title contender that mostly maintained the status quo this offseason was the Detroit Pistons, with whom Griffin played three-plus seasons and earned the last of his six career All-Star appearances. Led by MVP candidate Cade Cunningham, the Pistons finished with the best record in the Eastern Conference last season at 60-22 and appear poised to reach even greater heights this year.

Griffin said he's excited to see Cunningham continue his ascent to superstardom, and he expects the Pistons to put together a deeper playoff run after losing in the conference semifinals last season.

"I thought last year he took a huge step, which is outstanding, because he's been good since he came in. But he got to a point last year where he was completely dictating games. And especially at the point guard position, he's so big and can do so many different things. His handle is so good. He passes really, really well. And then the scoring on top of all that. So, he's obviously a big reason why that team was so good," he said. "But this year, it's another test. Last year, I felt like they were a young team that was just so fun to watch and playing pretty carefree in a way. And now this year will be that next step of like, 'Hey, we had regular season success last year. Now, we'll take it to the next level.' And I think they will."

Still, when it came to his early NBA Finals predictions, Griffin chose the last two NBA champions: the Oklahoma City Thunder and the New York Knicks, though he added that the San Antonio Spurs would be in the mix.

"I'm gonna give the benefit of the doubt to the Knicks," he said. "I think they reached a place last year where obviously everything was clicking, but also they just have such a great team balance and chemistry with guys who will step up and make big plays. You have Jalen Brunson, who is the unquestioned leader of that team. So I'm really curious to see their bounce-back season. So, let's go Knicks-Thunder. And that's hard to say because I love the Spurs, and I think they're going to be obviously really good again."

As arguably the greatest dunker of his generation, Griffin also weighed in on which player assumed the mantle in today's era, and he named Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards.

"Man, I think Ant is just one of those guys where you're just like, you never know what's gonna happen," he said. "And I love good in-game dunkers. Like, there's great dunk contest dunkers, and Ant can do both, but man, his in-game dunk package is so fun to watch because he's so smooth and he can kind of be shifty with it, whereas some guys, like myself, were more just like full speed ahead, downhill, you know what's coming, where he can kind of pop around and then just finish on somebody. So I'd give him the crown right now of best dunker."

Despite his high-flying feats, Edwards said long ago that he would never compete in the NBA Slam Dunk Contest during All-Star Weekend, and he's far from the only superstar who feels that way. Griffin, the 2011 Slam Dunk Contest champion, said he feels the NBA needs to remove all the bells and whistles if it wants to attract the most popular players to the annual showcase again.

"I think you strip it down. The dunk contest is about dunks. So I was having this conversation the other day. When I did the dunk contest, even then, we were in the back warming up. You come out, you line up, you're getting ready for intros. The intros happen. First person goes, second person goes, third person goes. I think I was maybe fourth that year. It had been 35, 45 minutes since I'd even warmed up, you know?" he said.

He continued: "So, because of all the theatrics, and I know there has to be some of it, but I would love to see it look a little bit more like a layup line... I think there's a happy medium between those two, where it's happening faster... and there's a little bit less waiting and set-up and theatrics to it. There's some things that just don't need that, and I think the dunk contest is one of them. So I hope that would entice some of the bigger names to just go do it because it's a little bit more relaxed and fun. But I don't know. You see some great dunks in the layup lines of the All-Star Game, that's what it should feel a little bit more like. You can still do the vote, like the point system and voting and all that, but make it a little less theatrical."

Despite his win 15 years ago, Griffin said he felt he fell victim to the theatrics during his infamous dunk over a Kia, which he revealed as his least favorite dunk from his iconic career.

"Honestly, man, I hate to say this, it's probably the dunk contest dunk. The Kia dunk. The plan was to catch low and do a windmill," he said. "And in the moment, because we've done the whole thing, like I just talked about, the car coming out and they were sort of encouraging us to come up with these [ideas]: 'Hey, what do you want to do? Do you want to bring out this?' So, I had the car idea, and I wanted just to get it done the first try, not have to keep going. So I just took the pass and ended up dunking it, but I think it would have been better and a little bit more of a higher degree of difficulty if I'd gotten the windmill down. But I can't really say it's one that I dislike, I just wish that I could do it again, you know?"

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton Talks Injury Rehab, Pacers' Doubters, More, 'Our Goal Is to Win a Championship'
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton possesses a "different perspective on life now" after missing an entire NBA season with a torn Achilles.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton possesses a "different perspective on life now" after missing an entire NBA season with a torn Achilles.

The veteran guard told ESPN's Jamal Collier there was one particular moment after undergoing surgery when he felt the full weight of the long road ahead. He was on vacation and had trouble moving around on his own power.

"Just having to come to terms with going from being on top of the world to the complete opposite of that in an instance," he said.

"It's such a crazy thing to say because it's a basketball injury that no matter what ... there's a time put on it. You know you're going to be good in that amount of time. We have the best doctors in the world, the best therapists, all those things. You know you're going to be good, but it's a scary thing."

Haliburton's injury obviously casts a big shadow over the upcoming season.

Achilles tears were once a career-altering injury, but Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant and two-time WNBA MVP Breanna Stewart both came back to maintain their previous levels on the court. Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum looked good in his limited run last year.

Haliburton's game may not have suffered that much.

Still, the Pacers are generally considered a contender that could struggle to replicate their run to the 2025 NBA Finals. They sit 16th in Bleacher Report's power rankings .

For Haliburton, there isn't any question about the team's expectations.

"I have my own internal expectations," he told Collier. "But our goal is to win a championship. That has never wavered."

The two-time All-Star added that he's trying to ignore the external forecasts.

"I don't look too much into it," he said. "Our whole team can relate to that. We've all felt that way one way or another."

Haliburton played 16 minutes in Indiana's preseason opener, a 123-112 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves. He finished with seven points on 3-of-8 shooting along with six assists.

It was an encouraging showing given how long the dynamic guard had been sidelined.

There's bound to be some rust once the regular season tips off. The preseason only reveals so much when the on-court intensity isn't the same compared to games that matter. Indy might be a little sluggish out of the gate.

It's hard to see how the Pacers are the favorites to win the Eastern Conference, but they've already proven how much they thrive in an underdog role.

articles.title: LeBron James Says 'Don't Write Off' SGA, Thunder as Title Contenders Ahead of 2026 NBA Season
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James implored fans to not "write off" the Oklahoma City Thunder despite their tough Western Conference Finals loss to the San Antonio Spurs last season.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James implored fans to not "write off" the Oklahoma City Thunder despite their tough Western Conference Finals loss to the San Antonio Spurs last season.

James made his comments during a 2026-27 season preview edition of his Mind the Game podcast with Basketball Hall of Famer Steve Nash (nine-minute mark).

"It's very important that we as fans of the game and the casuals don't write off OKC just yet," James began.

"Because you're so intrigued obviously with [San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama] and what [the Spurs] bring to the table and obviously the young guys, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle, you love what they bring to the game. And I love watching those guys. They're unbelievable, but we're quick to turn the page a lot faster than when we should.

"And I hope that we do not turn the page too fast on OKC. They got too much talent. They got too much experience. They were hungry last year and injuries always can affect some things. We always talk about the most important [thing] is being healthy. If those guys are healthy, they'll be right there. They'll be right there again. They're that good."

Led by now reigning back-to-back NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Oklahoma City took the 2024-25 NBA championship after winning a league-high 68 games. The Thunder also dominated the 2025-26 regular season with a league-high 64 victories.

OKC cruised through the first two rounds of the playoffs with a pair of sweeps against the Phoenix Suns and the Los Angeles Lakers. However, the Thunder then fell to the Spurs, who had beaten OKC in four of five games during the regular season, in seven.

OKC dealt with numerous injuries during that series. Of note, forward Jalen Williams, an All-NBA Third Teamer in 2024-25, played just 55 minutes over three games after suffering an aggravation of a left hamstring strain . Guard Ajay Mitchell suffered a right soleus (calf) strain and missed the final four games of the series.

We'll never know how the series would have turned out if Williams and Mitchell were more available, but San Antonio did a great job in its own right and certainly deserved to win that series.

Ultimately, OKC should be back in the mix. FanDuel Sportsbook gives OKC the shortest odds (+240) to win the NBA championship, with the Spurs (+270) right behind.

The Thunder begin the regular season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 with a rematch at the Spurs.

articles.title: LeBron James Responds to Anthony Edwards Trolling Him in Adidas Video for Signature Shoe
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards took a shot at the King, but it appears he missed.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards took a shot at the King, but it appears he missed.

After Edwards poked fun at Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James in an Adidas commercial for his latest signature shoe, James responded to the youngster during Tuesday's episode of his Mind the Game podcast (1:00 mark) and explained why he was unfazed by the barbs.

"First of all, I didn't watch the spot, because I don't watch anything from the stripes. Nothing. Love Ant to death, but I don't watch s--t from the stripes, I just don't. So I don't even know what he actually said." James told co-host Steve Nash. "... I think it said, 'He's old, too old, didn't want his knees to be cold.' But then I was like, 'But I went to Philly, Ant, so how are my knees gonna be warm in Philly?' ... He just read off the teleprompter."

James wasn't the only star that Edwards trolled in his commercial, which was premised on the 25-year-old hosting his own sketch show. Sixers star guard Jaylen Brown and Edwards' new teammate LaMelo Ball also caught some strays.

James and Edwards won't meet on the court for quite some time, as the Sixers and Timberwolves' first matchup this season is scheduled for Jan. 12.

articles.title: LeBron James Weighs In on Giannis, Bam Adebayo Pairing With Heat in Video, 'Damn Good'
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James praised the Miami Heat's pairing of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo ahead of the start of the 2026-27 NBA season on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James praised the Miami Heat's pairing of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo ahead of the start of the 2026-27 NBA season on Tuesday.

During his season preview on the Mind the Game podcast (beginning at the 19:50 mark) , James commented on the Giannis-Bam connection, saying, "My initial thought is, it's gonna be damn good."

James added, "Obviously, we've seen what Bam has been able to do over the past few seasons. He's actually started to shoot the three a lot more. ... We know with Giannis, he needs space. He wants space, he creates space. That's when he's really good, when he can attack the 45 or he can get to the gaps, and he has guys around him that create space. So, I think with Bam's ability to now shoot the three, I think that helps out a lot."

Miami made one of the biggest moves of the offseason when it sent Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis and four draft picks to the Milwaukee Bucks for Giannis and Bobby Portis.

Antetokounmpo is a two-time NBA MVP, one-time NBA champion, one-time NBA Finals MVP and future Hall of Famer who averages 29.1 points, 11.6 rebounds, 5.8 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.1 steals per game over the past nine seasons.

Adebayo is a star in his own right, as the 29-year-old center is a three-time All-Star coming off a season in which he averaged 20.1 points and 10.0 rebounds per game.

James expanded a bit more on his thoughts about the Heat, noting that he believes they will be "damn good" defensively thanks to Giannis, Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins and Davion Mitchell.

LeBron also praised Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra for knowing how to "put the pieces in the right position."

James played under Spoelstra for four seasons with the Heat from 2010 to 2014, reaching the NBA Finals four times and winning two championships.

Now, James is back in the Eastern Conference after signing with the Sixers and giving them arguably the best starting five in basketball between himself, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

However, the Giannis- and Bam-led Heat could prove to be a huge obstacle standing between the 76ers and a potential trip to the NBA Finals.

articles.title: LeBron James Says He 'Never Thought I Could Be Michael Jordan,' Resonated With Penny Hardaway
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James showcased his great respect and admiration of former Orlando Magic superstar guard (and four-time All-Star) Penny Hardaway during the latest edition of his Mind the Game podcast with Steve Nash.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James showcased his great respect and admiration of former Orlando Magic superstar guard (and four-time All-Star) Penny Hardaway during the latest edition of his Mind the Game podcast with Steve Nash.

Of note, James said his two favorite players growing up were Michael Jordan and Hardaway, saying the two made him "fall in love with the game of basketball."

However, James said he "never thought" he could be Jordan and specifically modeled his game specifically after Hardaway (and Basketball Hall of Famer Grant Hill) at the 43:29 mark.

"When I first started playing basketball, even though I loved Michael Jordan, I never thought I could be Michael Jordan. So I resonated with Penny more. Penny and Grant Hill helped shape my game...those two guys really helped shape my game, because I would watch them, and the way I was being taught the game by my little league coaches was exactly how Penny and Grant Hill was playing, so those guys helped shape my game. MJ inspired me to play the sport, but Penny and Grant Hill was the ones who actually shaped my game."

James, of course, now has a resume that has put him in the GOAT debate with Jordan. Entering his 24th season, the 41-year-old James has made 22 All-Star Games 21 All-NBA teams while winning four NBA titles, four NBA MVP awards and three Olympic gold medals.

As far as shaping James' game, it's easy to see Hardaway and Hill's impact. James is somewhat position-less and can fit into a variety of roles, including a point forward. That's the role Grant Hill once played when he starred for the Detroit Pistons, and Hardaway was one of the best passers and point guards in the NBA when he played for Orlando. James can play the point when needed, and he's fourth all time in assists with 12,016 .

James now begins a new chapter with the 76ers, who agreed a two-year deal. Year No. 24 begins Tuesday, Oct. 20 at the defending NBA champion New York Knicks.

articles.title: Pablo Laso tiene claro el fichaje que le falta al Real Madrid...y no de Baloncesto: "Ficharía a Rodri"
articles.standfirst: El técnico de Anadolu Efes analiza la Euroliga y a su ex equipo, en Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El técnico de Anadolu Efes analiza la Euroliga y a su ex equipo, en Radio MARCA
articles.body: Pablo Laso afronta una nueva etapa en el Anadolu Efes con la ambición de pelear por todos los títulos, aunque consciente de la enorme exigencia de la Euroliga. En una entrevista en 'El Programa de Ortega', el técnico vitoriano repasó la actualidad del baloncesto europeo, valoró la situación del Real Madrid y reivindicó el trabajo de los entrenadores españoles. Además, dejó clara su preferencia futbolística al ser preguntado por el jugador que ficharía para el conjunto blanco: "Ficharía a Rodri", respondió contundente. La lesión de Mike James ha supuesto un contratiempo importante para los planes de Laso, que ha tenido que reaccionar rápidamente en el mercado. El entrenador explicó que Cameron Payne ofrece características diferentes a las de la estrella ausente: "Es un jugador más base, más organizador de juego, pero menos 'killer'". Pese a perder a un referente dentro y fuera de la pista, Laso se mostró decidido a mantener la identidad competitiva del equipo: "Debemos ir siendo un equipo reconocible y competitivo desde el primer día". Sobre el Real Madrid, el técnico evitó sacar conclusiones precipitadas tras los cambios en la plantilla y en el banquillo. "Es muy pronto todavía para valorar a ningún equipo", advirtió, antes de mostrar su confianza en el potencial madridista. "Sigo viendo al Real Madrid un equipo muy competitivo todos los días. Creo que tiene una gran plantilla, muy buenos jugadores, un gran cuerpo técnico", afirmó. Laso considera que el club blanco está preparado para competir por los principales títulos, tanto en la Euroliga como en la Liga Endesa y la Copa. El entrenador también puso en valor la preparación de los técnicos españoles y su capacidad para gestionar grupos, más allá de los conocimientos tácticos. "Es un motivo de orgullo el hecho de que el entrenador español esté tan valorado", aseguró. Para Laso, el reconocimiento internacional responde a una combinación de preparación, conocimiento y capacidad para transmitir a los deportistas lo que necesitan. "Eso habla muy bien de cómo el entrenador español gestiona grupos", explicó, extendiendo esa valoración a otros deportes y a figuras destacadas del tenis como Juan Carlos Ferrero o Toni Nadal. En cuanto a la lucha por la Euroliga, Laso avisó de que conquistar el título exige superar un camino especialmente complicado. "Para ser campeón de la Euroliga significa, primero, entrar en 'playoff', luego, probablemente jugar un 'playoff' contra uno de los mejores equipos de Europa, ganarlo, y luego ir a una Final Four y ganar dos finales", resumió. El técnico recordó que la clasificación en la fase regular no garantiza el éxito y señaló que la igualdad obliga a mantener un alto nivel competitivo desde el inicio hasta mayo. También destacó que los equipos españoles pueden aspirar a los puestos de 'playoff'. Por último, Laso desveló cuál sería su fichaje ideal para el Real Madrid de fútbol: Rodri. Su elección responde a su debilidad por los centrocampistas capaces de organizar y liderar el juego. "A mí me gustan los jugadores que juegan y que organizan y que, de alguna manera, son líderes del equipo en algo", explicó. El técnico recordó la importancia que tuvieron Toni Kroos y Luka Modric para él: "Mi debilidad eran Kroos y Modric". Una declaración que resume el perfil de futbolista que más valora Laso y el tipo de liderazgo que, a su juicio, puede marcar la diferencia en un equipo.

articles.title: Knicks' $13M tenacious NBA champion likely to be traded amid uncertain future with organization
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are going to have to clear some room on the books. It looks like this young Knicks player could be the one to be traded.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks have several things to figure out this season, with some decisions potentially impacting the immediate future of the organization. Among the most notable are the contract extensions for Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns.

However, they aren't the only players eligible for extensions. Tyler Kolek and Miles "Deuce" McBride can also sign new deals.

"Per ESPN's Bobby Marks, the likes of Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek are all extension eligible, and the Knicks have until June 30 to get deals done with them," Bleacher Report's Mike Chiari wrote.

The biggest obstacle is the second apron, and owner James Dolan has made it clear that the Knicks will not exceed it. New York wants to extend Hart and Towns, but doing so will require careful financial planning to avoid putting the team in a difficult position.

"Bobby Marks says that scenarios have been presented to the Knicks where Josh Hart and KAT (both CAA) accept contracts that keep the Knicks under the second apron in 2027-28. He says KAT's comments Monday irked Dolan, which prompted today's statement," New York Post's Stefan Bondy wrote.

With those financial constraints in mind, the Knicks may need to trade a player to make the numbers work. The Stein Line's Marc Stein believes McBride could be dealt at some point during the season.

"One more important Knicks topic: Rival teams continue to describe McBride as a likely trade candidate as the season unfolds given the uncertainty surrounding his own Knicks future. McBride's $3.9 million salary for 2026-27, given the minimal salary that would take to match, is bound to generate interest from teams between now and the Feb. 11 trade deadline that want to acquire the 26-year-old before he hits free agency next June 30," Stein wrote.

McBride has spent his entire NBA career with New York after being drafted by the Knicks. However, the business side of the NBA can be complicated, and financial constraints can lead to difficult decisions.

McBride is currently under contract for $13 million. If the Knicks decide to move him, they could explore trade options while he still holds value around the league. With the team's financial situation becoming increasingly tight, a trade could be one way to create more flexibility.

articles.title: The heat is on 76ers’ Nick Nurse according to first head coach fired odds

articles.body:
BetOnline lists Nurse as the favorite to become the first NBA head coach fired this season, giving him +400 odds as Philadelphia prepares to compete for a championship with a star-studded roster.

Nurse leads a group of five coaches facing uncertainty entering the regular season. Sacramento Kings coach Doug Christie follows at +500, while Washington Wizards coach Brian Keefe sits at +600.

Houston Rockets coach Ime Udoka has +700 odds, and Cleveland Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson rounds out the top five at +800.

Nick Nurse faces heightened expectations with revamped 76ers roster

Philadelphia underwent a significant transformation this offseason, adding James and Brown to a core featuring Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

With James entering his 24th NBA season and Brown bringing championship experience, the 76ers have assembled one of the league's most talented starting groups.

However, the additions also place greater responsibility on Nurse to establish chemistry among four players accustomed to significant offensive roles.

Philadelphia must balance James' playmaking responsibilities with Maxey's scoring ability while incorporating Brown alongside Embiid.

Nurse, who guided the Toronto Raptors to their first NBA championship in 2019 , has experience managing a roster with title aspirations. His ability to integrate Philadelphia's new additions will be critical as the franchise pursues its first championship since 1983.

Although BetOnline's odds reflect speculation rather than any confirmed organizational plans, Nurse's position atop the list highlights the heightened expectations surrounding the 76ers.

With the regular season approaching, Philadelphia's performance could quickly determine whether Nurse remains under scrutiny or establishes the team as a legitimate championship contender.

articles.title: Lakers' Dalton Knecht gets brutal roster update as NBA future takes turn for the worse
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are going to have to make a roster decision very soon. Dalton Knecht is more than likely going to be the odd man out, but it also will...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are still one player over the allowed roster limit as training camp comes to an end. LA will have to decide how to get rid of at least one player.

The name expected to be let go is former first-round pick Dalton Knecht. Everything that has been said about him this preseason has been negative.

"Not a good sign for Knecht, whom multiple rival executives expect to be the odd man out as the Lakers look to trim their roster from 16 players on standard NBA deals to the league maximum of 15," California Post's Khobi Price wrote.

The only way for Knecht to avoid being waived is to be traded. There is a possibility he could be included in a consolidation trade to reduce the roster to 15 players.

"My understanding is a consolidation trade. Obviously, it would be two-for-one, three-for-one, or three-for-two is a little more complicated," Lakers insider Jovan Buha said. "So I think the most straightforward one would be two-for-one…And depending on the configuration of the trade, it could be a version of two of the back-end guys, let's say Dalton Knecht and Jaden Hardy, for a backup center."

However, if Knecht is waived, as many expect, his future in the NBA could become uncertain. There are not many teams with open roster spots.

"He's in a tough spot because most rosters are full, or actually, over-full," Buha said. "I just don't see a realistic landing spot where someone is gonna claim him off waivers or trade for him solo."

Things continue to look bleak for Knecht as he tries to prove he can be a productive player in the right system. His time in LA has not gone the way he hoped.

If Knecht is waived, he will have the opportunity to find a team that values him. The former first-round pick is still a good shooter who can contribute in that role, but finding the right opportunity will be key.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream WNBA Finals home games 3 and 4 moved to larger arena
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream were originally set to play WNBA Finals Games 3 and 4 at a 3,500-seat arena. The games have been moved to State Farm Arena.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream's home for multiple games during the 2026 WNBA Finals has been finalized.

The organization will play Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday, Oct. 21, with Game 4 topping off at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta , two people with direct knowledge of the situation told USA TODAY Sports. The people requested anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the decision publicly.

The date for Game 3 was changed from Thursday, Oct. 22 to accommodate the venue change, but the time remains the same with an 8 p.m. ET tipoff televised on USA Network. While Game 4 remains on Oct. 24, the tipoff time has moved to 1 p.m. ET from its original 3:30 p.m. to accommodate an Atlanta Hawks game at State Farm the same day. The Hawks game has been moved from an 8 p.m. ET start to an 8:30 p.m. tipoff.

A potential Game 6 (8 p.m. ET on Thursday, Oct. 29), is still currently scheduled to be at the Dream's home venue, Gateway Center Arena (3,500 seats). However, a person with knowledge of the situation told USA TODAY that additional discussions could happen to assess whether that facility will remain the venue of choice for Game 6.

After making the WNBA Finals, the Dream hoped to play at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. This year, the team hosted six regular-season contests and three postseason games at the venue. Still, initial talks to move Finals games were unsuccessful before Tuesday due to scheduling conflicts with a concert and two Atlanta Hawks games.

The Dream attempted to explore other venue options in the Atlanta area, such as Gas South Arena (up to 13,000 seats) and Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion (8,600 seats). Those efforts hit a roadblock.

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

On Tuesday, Oct. 6, the Dream announced they will call State Farm Arena home next year . Next season, the WNBA will move to 50 games , and State Farm will host the Dream's 25 home contests.

The Golden State Valkyries, who are hosting Games 1, 2, 5 and 7 of the Finals, will play at the Chase Center in San Francisco. Chase Center is the team's home throughout the WNBA regular season and has hosted multiple playoff games. Last year, Golden State's home playoff game relocated from the Chase Center because of a scheduling conflict with a tennis tournament. This year, after the Valkyries made the WNBA Finals, a concert, scheduled for the same day as Game 2 (Oct. 19), was moved .

"We will not play a game outside of Chase Center this postseason," Valkyries team president Jess Smith said recently. "Our ownership group (has) been committed to that. ... We understand the prioritization."

Atlanta advanced to the Finals after sweeping the Washington Mystics in the first round, and the New York Liberty in the semifinals. The Dream returned to the Finals for the first time since the 2013 season. The franchise is 0-9 all-time in Finals games.

articles.title: 76ers’ LeBron James sends warning to Thunder doubters amid Spurs’ rapid ascension
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs beat the Oklahoma City Thunder in the Western Conference Finals 4-3 last season in what was one of the most entertaining playoff series...
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs beat the Oklahoma City Thunder in the Western Conference Finals 4-3 last season in what was one of the most entertaining playoff series in recent memory. Much of the credit went to Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs' young core, specifically the likes of Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle.

LeBron James believes that the Thunder, as a result, are being underestimated as far as projections for the upcoming season are concerned. Speaking to Steve Nash on Mind the Game, the Philadelphia 76ers star claimed that NBA fans should not be so quick to write the Thunder off, per a post on X by NBA Courtside.

"I think it's very important that we as fans of the game and the casuals don't write off OKC just yet," he said. "I mean, because you're so intrigued with obviously Victor and rightfully so and what they bring to the table and obviously the young guys, Dylan Harper, you know, and Stephon Castle you love what they bring to the game. And I love watching those guys. They're unbelievable, but we quick to turn the page a lot faster than we should."

Wembanyama's rise in the NBA has been extremely drastic despite the Spurs' main man being limited to just 46 games in the 2024-25 season. He won the Defensive Player of the Year award last season and finished third in MVP voting, and is largely expected to help San Antonio mount regular title challenges in the coming seasons.

The Spurs have also made the right moves in recent offseasons and have an extremely talented young core that is only going to improve alongside Wemby in the coming time. At the same time, the Thunder not only have a similarly talented roster, they were also the No. 1 team in the West last season after finishing the regular season with a 64-18 record, pipping the Spurs by two wins.

They may have come up short against San Antonio when it mattered the most, but actually led the series twice before the Spurs won the final two games to qualify for the Finals. There is little that OKC continues to one of the top teams in the NBA, and not many will be surprised if they end up putting together another title run in the coming campaign.

articles.title: Warriors’ Draymond Green calls out NBA refs as total phonies over new points of emphasis
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors veteran forward Draymond Green expressed skepticism about NBA referees consistently enforcing the league’s new emphasis on offensive pl...
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors veteran forward Draymond Green expressed skepticism about NBA referees consistently enforcing the league's new emphasis on offensive players using their off-arm to create separation, arguing that such calls typically disappear once the regular season begins.

As the Warriors prepare for the 2026-27 NBA season , Green addressed the league's preseason officiating adjustments during the latest episode of The Draymond Green Show, warning fellow defenders against expecting the changes to last.

"The NBA refs started to enforce the off-arm push-off rule in the preseason. Quite honestly, as a defensive player I would tell you all, don't bank on this, don't waste your time thinking like 'oh man, like imma see them calling this now' like I'm telling you, these types of rules here that's going against the offense, they call them in the preseason and then when the season starts, that sh*t just fade away."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Green's criticism centers on what he believes is a longstanding inconsistency in how officials enforce rules that could benefit defensive players.

The four-time NBA champion suggested that the league's emphasis on limiting offensive push-offs will ultimately give way to its preference for allowing star scorers to operate without additional restrictions.

"Great offensive players are going to come down, bam – get out of here, shoot they shot, get they basket, everything [is] going to go the other way. These types of rules here in my 15 years, they don't stand. Apparently there's supposed to be a freedom of movement where you know how they just be grabbing Steph and hugging on him? That's supposed to be a foul. Guess what? Freedom of movement been a thing and we've seen Steph Curry not get those fouls."

Draymond Green points to Stephen Curry as example of inconsistent NBA officiating

Green specifically referenced the physical defensive coverage that Warriors superstar Stephen Curry frequently encounters, arguing that existing freedom-of-movement rules have not consistently protected his longtime teammate.

The NBA's freedom-of-movement guidelines are intended to prevent defenders from illegally restricting offensive players through holding, grabbing and other forms of contact.

However, Green believes the inconsistent enforcement of those rules offers little reason to expect the league's renewed attention to offensive push-offs to produce lasting changes.

Rather than relying on referees to penalize offensive players, Green explained that he plans to adjust his defensive positioning to counter the contact.

"So, guess what? I ain't going to hold my breath on that one either. So, me as a defender, I got to learn to time up when that guy is about to deliver that blow so I can lean my chest forward a little bit so when he deliver the off-arm I don't go to far back. I may go from this lean back to my natural position and I can still climb up a little bit and contest the shot. Ultimately, as a defender that's my mindset because I'm not banking on them doing nothing against the offense. It ain't just never been a thing."

With Golden State preparing for another season built around Curry and its veteran core, Green's comments highlight his frustration with officiating standards that he believes consistently favor offensive players.

Whether referees maintain their preseason emphasis on offensive push-offs remains to be seen once the regular season begins.

articles.title: The lost art that’s going to be a game-changer for Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES – The top priority for the Los Angeles Lakers during the offseason was to acquire a franchise center. They believe they’ve found one in Walker Ke...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – The top priority for the Los Angeles Lakers during the offseason was to acquire a franchise center. They believe they've found one in Walker Kessler. But a starting center was not the only concern for the Lakers' frontcourt, a backup center was a requirement as well. Whoever plays the reserve five role for the team is likely going to be matchup based, but the Lakers have a one strong option in veteran big man Kevon Looney .

Kevon Looney was one of the Lakers' later free agent signings after their initial splurge, and the veteran center brings a specific skill set that compliments the team's main stars in Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves . Doncic in particular is a fan of a more structured offense involving pick and rolls, and Looney has been among the best screen-setters in the NBA.

For the first 10 years of his career, the former UCLA standout played alongside two of the best players in league history as far as utilizing screens in Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson. While setting a proper screen has become a bit of a lost art in today's game, Looney believes he is one of the remaining players who can adequately free up his shooters via proper pick.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It is [a lost art], but there's some great screeners in the league and I feel like I'm one of them. It's different for each player. Every scorer wants a screen set a certain way. So for me, just kind of learning what they want and executing it to the best of m ability," Looney said following Lakers practice on Oct. 10. "I'm kind of learning fast what Luka and AR want. There's still room for improvement, it's the preseason, but we're starting good with that chemistry."

Last season was the first that Looney played away from the Warriors. He signed as a free agent with the New Orleans Pelicans in the 2025 offseason, but did not play much amid the team's disappointing year. He appeared in only 21 games, and made the decision to move on in the summer.

The two-time NBA champion still has gas left in the tank, and it's not just on the court where is value is seen. Looney has been in the league for a while now and brings a wealth of experience and knowledge that the younger players on the Lakers' roster can benefit from. Take Walker Kessler for example. The fifth-year big man has been limited in training camp due to a finger injury, but in his short time around Looney, he's already picked up quite a bit.

"His screening ability is second to none," Kessler said after Lakers practice on Oct. 11. "His positioning, obviously his size, you can't really teach that, but his ability to be in the right spot at the right time, get in the way of the defender, I've definitely been noticing that. And being like, how can I apply that to my own game."

With Kessler sidelined for the first three preseason games , Lakers head coach JJ Redick has gone with Looney as the starting center in two of those three games. In his first outing , he responded with a team-high nine rebounds in 18 minutes. In his second start, he had five rebounds in 17 minutes. That was tied with Austin Reaves for second on the team, and behind only Jarred Vanderbilt's six boards.

Looney's been able to have solid longevity in the NBA, and for him, the key was learning how to play a role. He knew coming into the league, he wasn't going to have the same type of freedom that he did in college. He had to adapt and learn how to fill a niche. And now that he's one of the veteran guys, he takes it upon himself to impart that wisdom onto younger players looking to gain footing in the NBA.

"That's one of the hardest things as a young guy coming into the NBA. You're used to being the man of your team, now you come into a situation … a lot of times there's gonna be a guy that's already established as a superstar. You got to learn how to play off him, and it's not easy to adjust to," Looney said. "You got to wait your turn and everybody's not good at being patient and waiting and don't know how to work when they don't have the ball in their hands.

"It's always difficult, but we try to teach all the young guys coming in … talking about learning how to be great in your role and how to be a star in your role, and you can make a lot of money in this league."
